recipes.title: Aunt Elizabeth's Chicken Paprikash
steps: Cut the chicken breasts, onion, and bell pepper into bite-sized pieces.
In a large skillet, melt the butter together with the olive oil over medium-high heat until the mixture foams.
Add the chicken, onion, and bell pepper to the skillet and sauté for about 5 minutes until the chicken is thoroughly cooked.
Sprinkle in the paprika and black pepper, stirring continuously for 1 minute.
Pour in the white wine (or chicken broth), lemon juice, and tomato paste; bring to a gentle boil and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Lower the heat to low, stir in the sour cream, and simmer gently for 3 minutes without boiling.
Serve warm spooned generously over separately cooked noodles.
recipes.swaps: Margarine can replace butter; chicken broth can replace white wine; tomato sauce can replace tomato paste; green or red bell pepper can be used.
recipes.notes: Cook noodles separately in boiling water according to package directions before plating.

recipes.title: Healthy Chicken Broccoli Quinoa
steps: Dice the chicken breasts into 1-inch cubes and season liberally with salt and pepper.
In a large skillet or pot with a tight-fitting lid, heat the olive oil and 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat.
Add the seasoned chicken pieces and cook for about 5 minutes until cooked through, then transfer to a plate and set aside.
Melt the remaining tablespoon of butter in the same pan, then add the diced onion and celery, cooking for 3 to 4 minutes until softened.
Stir in the minced garlic, dried thyme, dried rosemary, and crushed red pepper flakes, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the uncooked quinoa and chicken broth, turn the heat to high, and bring the liquid to a boil.
Lower the heat to low, cover tightly with the lid, and simmer for about 15 minutes until most of the broth is absorbed by the quinoa.
Place the broccoli florets on top of the quinoa and return the cooked chicken to the skillet, then cover and cook for another 5 minutes until the broccoli is tender and the liquid is fully absorbed.
Stir in the lemon juice, sprinkle with fresh parsley, and serve warm directly from the skillet.
recipes.notes: Cooked in a single large skillet or pot with a tight-fitting lid.
